title: The Django ORM: Querying Data
description: Learn how to create, retrieve, update, and delete records using Python code.

slides.title: What is an ORM? 🤖
slides.content:
**Object‑Relational Mapper (ORM)** – it lets you interact with your database using Python objects, not SQL.

Django automatically translates Python method calls into SQL statements. For example, `Post.objects.all()` becomes `SELECT * FROM blog_post`.

slides.title: Creating Records
slides.content: Use the model's `save()` method or the `create()` method:
slides.codeSnippet:
# Option 1: Create and save
post = Post(title="My First Post", content="Hello world!")
post.save()

# Option 2: Create directly
Post.objects.create(title="Another Post", content="More content")

quizData.question: Which method would you use to get all objects from a model?
quizData.explanation: `all()` returns a QuerySet containing all rows. `filter()` returns a subset, and `get()` returns a single object.

slides.title: Retrieving Data
slides.codeSnippet:
# Get all posts
all_posts = Post.objects.all()

# Get a single post by primary key (id)
post = Post.objects.get(id=1)

# Filter by field value
recent_posts = Post.objects.filter(published_date__year=2025)

# Chain filters
posts = Post.objects.filter(is_published=True).exclude(title__contains="draft")

slides.title: Field Lookups 🔍
slides.content:
Django provides double‑underscore lookups for field conditions:
- `title__contains` – case‑sensitive containment
- `title__icontains` – case‑insensitive
- `published_date__gte` – greater than or equal
- `published_date__lte` – less than or equal
- `author__name__startswith` – can follow relationships

slides.title: Updating and Deleting
slides.content:
# Update
post = Post.objects.get(id=1)
post.title = "Updated Title"
post.save()

# Bulk update
Post.objects.filter(is_published=False).update(is_published=True)

# Delete
post.delete()
Post.objects.filter(title__contains="spam").delete()

quizData.question: What is the correct way to delete all posts that have 'spam' in the title?
quizData.explanation: `filter()` returns a QuerySet; calling `delete()` on it deletes all matching rows.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `get()` only when you're sure one object exists

`get()` raises `DoesNotExist` if no object is found and `MultipleObjectsReturned` if more than one. For safe retrieval, use `filter().first()`.
